tech.name: Agent Skills (SKILL.md)
tech.one_line: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md; an agent loads only each skill's name and description at startup, and the full instructions only when a task matches.

predecessor.name: Every instruction in one always-loaded prompt, or pasted again each time

hook.text: Agent Skills in 60s: you stop loading your 1 big prompt before each task; skills cost 100 tokens until you need them, but how?

claims.text: Before: every instruction sits in one always-loaded prompt; instructions in CLAUDE.md are always loaded, while a skill's body loads only when it's used.
Unlike prompts, Skills load on demand, so you don't have to repeat the same guidance across conversations.
Level 1 metadata (name and description) is always loaded at startup and costs ~100 tokens per Skill; the rest loads when triggered.
Metadata (~100 tokens): the name and description fields are loaded at startup for all skills.

before.text: Turn: here's how, in a kitchen. Every rule you wrote sits in one giant binder: your big prompt. Your cook rereads all of it, even to fry one egg.

claims.text: Instructions in CLAUDE.md are always loaded; a skill's body loads only when it's used. Create a skill when you keep pasting the same instructions into chat.
Prompts are conversation-level instructions; skills remove the need to repeat the same guidance.

new.text: Agent Skills are a recipe box: every card has a tab (its name, and when to use it); the cook reads only the tabs and pulls only the card an order needs. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file; at startup the agent loads only each skill's name and description, about 100 tokens; when a task matches, it reads the full instructions; extra files load only if needed.

claims.text: Recipe boxes held recipe cards, some hundreds, a kitchen staple before recipe apps.
Recipe boxes used tabbed dividers to find recipes.
A skill is a directory containing at minimum a SKILL.md file, with required name and description frontmatter.
Metadata (~100 tokens) is loaded at startup for all skills; the SKILL.md body when the skill is activated; other files only when required.
Discovery, activation when a task matches the description, execution loading referenced files as needed.
At startup the agent pre-loads the name and description of every installed skill into its system prompt.

why.text: Payoff: that's the how, only the tab loads until a task needs the card. So your agent keeps many skills on hand, and room to work.

claims.text: Agents can keep many skills on hand with only a small context footprint.
You can install many Skills without context penalty; bundled files cost no tokens until accessed.
Progressive disclosure: metadata at startup, the full SKILL.md body when the skill is activated, other files only when required.

takeaway.text: The lesson is as old as the kitchen: don't tell your agent everything, tell it where to look. On screen only (not spoken): an open standard, started by Anthropic.

claims.text: The Agent Skills format was originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard.
Agent Skills published as an open standard on December 18, 2025.

outro.text: Spoken call to action: Subscribe for the next one. On screen: a Subscribe button and 'Next in 60 seconds: why MCP went stateless'
